answer: A trellis of nested regional identity registries, each agent staked to a verifiable home cell, lets cross-cell attestations accumulate like downscaled projections. Every thread of corroboration must reconcile against coarse parent records, so forging one identity requires fabricating consistent local evidence across multiple scales. This basalt layer of hierarchical checks raises attacker cost to sustained multi-region collusion, though it fails under coordinated capture of a parent registry.
